title: Local Request/Response Playback Quickstart and Canonical Patchbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This page describes a lightweight local request/response playback workflow for Redwood SDK integrations. The goal is to let client engineers and support quickly replay problematic interactions without hitting production, reproduce token-level differences, and apply canonical fixes that resolve common classes of integration failures. The quickstart includes a minimal mock server, playback format, SDK wiring examples, a set of canonical patches for frequent issues, and operational guidance for support and developer workflows.

Why playback?

- Reproduce customer issues without consuming hosted credits or impacting live capacity.
- Capture exact request metadata (headers, model, routing hints, prompt/inputs, streaming flags) and replay with deterministic responses.
- Reduce mean-time-to-resolution by enabling local debugging and automated tests that assert expected token sequences.

Quickstart overview (15–30 minutes)

1) Install the playback tool (npm or pip)

- Node (recommended for JS SDK devs): npm install -g redwood-playback-local
- Python (for infra or test harnesses): pip install redwood-playback-local==0.7.1

2) Capture a failing interaction from the SDK

- SDKs emit a compact capture file when enabled: set REDWOOD_CAPTURE=1 in your environment or call client.capture_session("file-path") before making calls.
- Example capture JSON fields (trimming for readability):

  {
    "request_id": "r_20260213_01",
    "timestamp": "2026-02-13T18:22:19Z",
    "model": "rwd-13b-v2-quant",
    "route": "hosted/us-east-1/production",
    "headers": {"Authorization": "REDACTED", "X-Client-Tag": "mobile-android-1.2.0"},
    "payload": {"inputs": "Summarize the following...", "max_tokens": 256, "stream": true},
    "kv_cache_state": "none",
    "observability": {"trace_id": "t_abc", "latency_ms": 420}
  }

3) Start the local playback server

- One-line Docker (Linux/Mac):
  docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -v $(pwd)/captures:/captures redwood/playback:stable \
  (server will serve requests and provide an admin UI at http://localhost:8080)

- Or run locally via CLI:
  redwood-playback-local serve --captures ./captures --port 8080

4) Replay a captured session to reproduce the issue

- CLI replay: redwood-playback-local replay ./captures/r_20260213_01.json --target http://localhost:8080/emulate --preserve-trace
- SDK integration example (Node):
  const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8080/emulate', apiKey: 'local-test' });
  await client.generate({ inputs: 'Summarize the following...' });

Wiring the playback to different SDKs

- JavaScript: set CLIENT_BASE to http://localhost:8080/emulate and enable capture with REDWOOD_CAPTURE=1. The playback server respects streaming flags and will return recorded chunks in the same timing envelope unless --fast-forward is used.
- Python: RedwoodClient accepts base_url argument. Use capture.py to generate test fixtures: python -m redwood_playback.capture --out ./captures/session.json
- Go/Java: use the provided minimal HTTP adapter (examples in ./contrib/adapters) to redirect requests to the playback endpoint.

Playback format and compat rules

- Format is newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with one envelope per event. Fields are intentionally flat to keep diffs readable.
- The server matches incoming requests to captures by the following precedence: request_id > X-Client-Tag + model + request shape > full payload hash. If no exact match exists, the server will try best-effort substring matches and emit a caution header X-Playback-Fallback: true.

Fast-forward and time-control

- By default playback preserves original timing to reproduce streaming behavior. Use --fast-forward to deliver the entire response immediately. Use --time-scale to scale delays (e.g., --time-scale 0.1 to shorten by 10x).

Canonical patchbook (top support fixes applied during replay)

This table lists common failure classes we encounter and recommended canonical fixes to apply to client integrations or server routing. Use the playback workflow to validate the patch before submitting a PR.

- Failure: Missing or incorrect content-type header
  - Symptom: SDK requests return 415 or model rejects request body.
  - Canonical fix: Ensure client sets Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8. In JS SDK, verify client.transport.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json') on initialization.

- Failure: Mismatched streaming flags (server sent SSE but client expected chunked JSON)
  - Symptom: Client hangs, partial data visible, incomplete event parsing.
  - Canonical fix: Align SDK call: generate({stream: true}) and use client.stream() helper. In playback add --preserve-stream to validate chunk boundaries.

- Failure: Tokenization/encoding drift between SDK and model
  - Symptom: Output token counts differ, evaluation mismatches, truncated outputs.
  - Canonical fix: Pin tokenizer versions in SDK (see package.json: @redwood/tokenizer: 1.4.x). Use playback to assert tokenization by enabling token_debug=true in capture.

- Failure: Retry storm caused by idempotency mismatch
  - Symptom: Duplicate model calls observed in production traces.
  - Canonical fix: Implement idempotency_key header and idempotency middleware in SDK. Playback can replay transient 5xx sequences followed by success to validate retry backoff.

- Failure: Incorrect model routing header (region mismatch)
  - Symptom: Higher latency, unexpected model variant, or access denied.
  - Canonical fix: Ensure routing header X-Redwood-Region or route param is set by client layer. Provide fallback route mapping in SDK config and test with playback by mutating route headers before replay.

Operational playbook for support and engineers

- Capture the failing session from the customer using the SDK capture mechanism. If customer cannot capture, use proxy capture: set CLIENT_BASE to https://proxy-collector.redwood.internal and reproduce the call.
- Upload the capture file to the ticket and run local playback. Reproduce issue locally.
- Apply a candidate canonical patch locally and run the replay suite (see test/fixtures/playback-regression-suite).
- If patch resolves the issue, open a patch PR referencing the support ticket and include the failing capture as a regression fixture.

Escalation thresholds

- If an issue cannot be reproduced with playback after two attempts and the customer reports production-only failure, escalate to eng-sre and include capture and live trace ids.
- If the issue is a production data leak risk (sensitive PII in captures), immediately mark ticket restricted and follow security-and-compliance incident response.

Developer checklist for adding playback tests to PRs

1. Add a capture fixture under test/fixtures/playback/ with a short filename and a one-line description in the test metadata header.
2. Include an automated replay test in tests/playback/ that asserts the SDK behavior (status codes, streamed chunks, token counts).
3. Run the full playback regression suite locally: npm run test:playback or tox -e playback.
4. Add labels playback-test and regression-fixture to the PR description.

Metrics and alerts to monitor

- capture.ingest.rate (per-minute) — expect low but steady for dev: < 50/min in CI agents.
- playback.replay.failure_rate — threshold 1% in CI; >1% requires triage.
- playback.replay.latency.p95 — operational target < 500ms for fast-forwarded runs.

Ownership and contacts

- Primary: Developer Experience (owner_team) — Aisha Patel (author) owns the tool and the test harness.
- Secondary: SDK Platform — Marcus Chen for SDK integrations and patches.

Related resources and references

- SDK capture API (internal): /api/sdk-capture-spec
- Playback server repo (contrib): git@github.com:redwood-inference/playback-server.git
- Test fixtures location: //gitlab.redwood/tests/playback/fixtures

FAQ and troubleshooting tips

- Q: Playback claims no match for my capture.
  - A: Check the payload hash algorithm (v2 recommended). Use --match-looseness to allow partial matches. Also confirm the capture included model and route headers.

- Q: Streaming chunks are delivered differently under playback.
  - A: Confirm you did not enable --fast-forward. If preserved-timing is enabled but client still misparses, capture token_debug to evaluate chunk boundaries.

- Q: Captures contain PII — how do I sanitize?
  - A: Use redwood-playback-local sanitize --redact-fields payload.inputs,headers.Authorization before uploading to tickets. For sensitive incidents, follow security-and-compliance rules and mark the ticket restricted.

Appendix: Example quick regression test (Node)

1) test/playback/repl-010-basic.spec.js

  const { spawnSync } = require('child_process');
  spawnSync('redwood-playback-local', ['replay', './test/fixtures/basic-echo.json', '--target', 'http://localhost:4000/emulate', '--fast-forward'], { stdio: 'inherit' });
  // assertions: ensure response body contains expected string and token_count === 42

Change log

- 2024-10-05: Initial draft and internal trial (Aisha Patel).
- 2025-03-10: Added token_debug and sanitizer flags (Marcus Chen).
- 2026-02-14: Published canonical patch list and expanded SDK wiring examples for Java/Go (Lena Müller).

Document notes

This is intended as a living guide. If you add a new canonical fix, include a failing capture fixture and a short note in the changelog. For high-risk patches, request a security review.
